result: The authors generated a mouse model expressing the p53Y217C mutation (murine equivalent of human p53Y220C) using homologous recombination in ES cells with a conditional targeting vector containing LoxP-flanked transcriptional stops. The construct was verified by sequencing and showed similar p53 mRNA levels between WT and Trp53YC/YC MEFs.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge the generation and characterization of the Y217C mouse model without raising concerns. One reviewer states 'the generation and characterization of Y220C mice (Y217C in the mouse allele)' as a notable finding, and another notes 'the generation and characterization of a knock-in mouse strain expressing the p53 Y217C hot-spot mutation.' The quality of the work is described as 'well done and good.'

result: The p53Y217C mutation resulted in loss of canonical p53 functions including loss of DNA damage responses, inability to transactivate p21 and Mdm2, predominantly cytoplasmic localization, loss of cell cycle arrest and apoptosis upon DNA damage, and no dominant-negative effect in heterozygous cells.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly accept these findings as demonstrating loss of p53 function. One reviewer notes 'the homozygous mutant cells and mice reflect the typical loss-of-p53 functions, as expected' and another states 'Y217C may not function as a dominant negative' based on similar tumor formation in heterozygotes. The editor describes this as having 'an exceptional level of evidence.'

result: Trp53YC/YC fibroblasts exhibited increased chromosomal instability compared to Trp53-/- cells, with more frequent chromosome breaks, radial chromosomes, and double-minute chromosomes, indicating a gain-of-function that promotes chromosomal instability.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding without criticism. One reviewer explicitly notes 'elevated metastasis in the homozygous context (as noted with several hot-spot mutations)' and describes the Y217C mutation as displaying 'gain-of function (GOF) properties.' The work is described as 'well controlled and quite well done.'

result: Trp53YC/YC male mice died faster than Trp53-/- males (all dead by 7 months vs >20% alive at 7 months) and developed more aggressive and invasive thymic lymphomas with metastases to lungs, spleen, liver, and kidneys, indicating oncogenic properties of the p53Y217C mutation.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these findings as key results. One reviewer states 'the authors find that homozygous Y217C mice die faster than p53 -/- mice, and that the lymphomas in the Y217C mice were more aggressive and invasive.' Another notes 'elevated metastasis in the homozygous context' as evidence of GOF. The editor describes the work as having 'fundamental significance.'

result: Trp53+/YC and Trp53+/- heterozygous mice exhibited similar spontaneous tumor onset and spectrum, with most developing sarcomas during their second year of life, indicating no dominant-negative effect of p53Y217C over wildtype p53 for spontaneous tumorigenesis.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly accept this finding. One reviewer notes 'similar tumor formation in Y217C/+ and p53 +/- mice, suggesting that Y217C may not function as a dominant negative.' Another states 'this mutation does not appear to exhibit any dominant-negative effects' based on 'absence of differences in overall survival and tumor predisposition of the heterozygous mice.' No concerns are raised about this conclusion.

result: Trp53YC/YC mice showed severe female-specific perinatal lethality with only 1 female for 19-22 males at weaning, explained by high frequency (38.5%) of exencephaly in female embryos at E12.5-E16.5 (much higher than 0-8% in Trp53-/- embryos) and death of most female neonates before P2, indicating teratogenic effects of the p53Y217C mutation.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these findings as notable results. One reviewer states 'Y217C mice that have been backcrossed to C57Bl/6 for five generations show decreased female pup births due to exencephaly, a known defect in p53 -/- mice' and notes 'increased female neonatal death.' Another reviewer notes 'a severe reduction in the female 217/217 homozygous progeny, significantly more than that observed with the p53 null mice, due to exencephaly' and that the authors 'conclude that the Y217C mutation also has additional, non-cancer related GOFs.'

result: Trp53YC/YC males were fertile, but the two Trp53YC/YC adult females that mated and became pregnant both exhibited dystocia with extended labor (>24 hr) and had to be euthanized, indicating additional effects of the p53Y217C mutation on female reproduction beyond loss of canonical p53 activities.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about these observations. The findings are presented as part of the comprehensive characterization of the model, and one reviewer notes the mutation has 'additional, non-cancer related GOFs.' The overall work is described as 'well-conducted' with no specific critiques of the dystocia observations.

result: RNA-seq analysis of thymi from 8-week-old males revealed 81.5% of 717 differentially expressed genes indicated loss-of-function in p53Y217C, but also genes suggesting GOF/SOF. Comparative analysis of Trp53YC/YC vs Trp53-/- thymi showed 192 differentially expressed genes with significant enrichment for inflammation-related genes (Ccl17, Ccl9, Ccr3, Cxcl10, S100a8, S100a9) that were significantly increased in Trp53YC/YC cells.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these findings. One reviewer states 'the authors then perform RNA seq on thymi of Y217C homozygotes compared to p53 -/-, and they suggest that these differentially expressed genes may explain the increased tumorigenesis in Y217C mice.' Another notes 'Transcriptomic analyses of thymi found additional gene signature differences between p53 null and the Y217C strains, indicative of novel target gene activation, associated with inflammation.' The conclusions are described as 'reasonably well justified.'

result: GSEA revealed 13 gene sets significantly enriched in Trp53YC/YC cells (NES>2), including three immunity-related sets (antimicrobial peptides, chemokine receptors bind chemokines, defensins), five related to mitochondria function, three related to chromatin plasticity, and enrichment of NC-NF-κB signaling, consistent with inflammatory response and potentially contributing to accelerated tumorigenesis.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these transcriptomic findings without criticism. One reviewer notes the data are 'indicative of novel target gene activation, associated with inflammation' and states the 'conclusions are reasonably well justified.' The overall characterization is described as having 'good' quality with the work being 'well done.'

result: Treatment of pregnant females with the anti-inflammatory drug supformin (LCC-12) resulted in a fivefold increase in the female to male ratio for Trp53YC/YC weaned animals (from 0.045 to 0.23), reaching a value indistinguishable from Trp53-/- weaned animals, suggesting that reducing inflammation in developing Trp53YC/YC female embryos may increase their viability.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about this experimental intervention or its interpretation. The finding is presented as part of the comprehensive characterization linking inflammation to the developmental phenotypes. One reviewer notes the work is 'well controlled and quite well done,' and the editor describes it as having 'an exceptional level of evidence.'

result: Neurospheres from Trp53YC/YC females showed decreased Xist expression and increased expression of X-linked genes (Maob, Pls3, Usp9x) compared to WT, similar to Trp53-/- neurospheres, suggesting aberrant X chromosome inactivation may contribute to underrepresentation of Trp53YC/YC females, though defects did not appear more pronounced than in Trp53-/- neurospheres.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the correlation with decreased Xist expression without raising concerns. One reviewer explicitly notes the authors 'show a correlation with decreased Xist expression' as part of the findings. The data are presented as supporting evidence for mechanisms underlying female lethality, and no critiques of these measurements are raised.

result: Mdm2-/- Trp53YC/YC and Mdm4-/- Trp53YC/YC viable mice of both sexes were identified, consistent with major loss of canonical WT p53 activities. However, the female to male ratio for Trp53YC/YC animals appeared markedly increased in Mdm4 haploinsufficient (4/15) or null (1/6) backgrounds but only marginally in Mdm2 haploinsufficient (1/11) or null (1/11) backgrounds.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about these genetic rescue experiments. The findings are presented as additional evidence for loss of canonical p53 function and potential mechanisms for improved female survival. The overall work is described as 'well-conducted' and having 'good' quality.

result: The p53Y217C mutation leads to loss of many canonical WT p53 activities (including transactivation of Bbc3, Cdkn1a, Zmat3) and can rescue embryonic lethality from Mdm2/Mdm4 deficiency, consistent with complete or near complete LOF. However, the mutation also exhibits oncogenic effects with accelerated tumorigenesis in Trp53YC/YC mice, potentially through promoting inflammation.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly accept these summary conclusions. One reviewer states 'the homozygous mutant cells and mice reflect the typical loss-of-p53 functions, as expected' and notes 'the Y217C mutation also appears to display gain-of function (GOF) properties.' The editor describes the work as having 'fundamental significance and has an exceptional level of evidence for the role of a mutant p53 in regulation of tumorigenesis.'

result: The p53Y217C mutation promotes inflammation with oncogenic effects in males (accelerated tumorigenesis) and teratogenic effects in females (neural tube defects, perinatal lethality, dystocia). Common mechanisms involving inflammation may contribute to both phenotypes, and the GOF of this hotspot mutant p53 may not be limited to oncogenic effects.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these overarching conclusions. One reviewer notes the authors 'conclude that the Y217C mutation also has additional, non-cancer related GOFs' and that 'this property has been well described and attributed to p53 functional impairment, the authors conclude that the Y217C has additional properties in accelerating the phenotype.' The conclusions are described as 'reasonably well justified' and the work as having 'fundamental significance.'
